claim: Context is information linked to a situation that can guide behavior.
source: Context is information linked to a situation that can guide behavior.
evidence: This is a definitional statement provided in the abstract without supporting data in the manuscript.

claim: In the brain, context is encoded by sensory processing and can later be retrieved from memory.
source: In the brain, context is encoded by sensory processing and can later be retrieved from memory.
evidence: This statement is supported by the experimental findings showing encoding and retrieval network structures (Structures 3 and 4).

claim: Using hemisphere-wide, high-density electrocorticography, large-scale neuronal activity was measured from monkeys observing videos of agents interacting in situations with different contexts.
source: Using hemisphere-wide, high-density electrocorticography, we measured large-scale neuronal activity from monkeys observing videos of agents interacting in situations with different contexts.
evidence: The methods section describes the use of 128-channel ECoG arrays and the experimental paradigm.

claim: Five context-related network structures were extracted including a bottom-up network during encoding and, seconds later, cue-dependent retrieval of the same network with the opposite top-down connectivity.
source: We extracted five context-related network structures including a bottom-up network during encoding and, seconds later, cue-dependent retrieval of the same network with the opposite top-down connectivity.
evidence: PARAFAC analysis identified five structures with distinct functional, temporal, and anatomical properties as shown in Figures 4 and 5.

claim: Context is represented in the cortical network as distributed communication structures with dynamic information flows.
source: These findings show that context is represented in the cortical network as distributed communication structures with dynamic information flows.
evidence: The five network structures show distributed anatomical patterns with time-varying connectivity as demonstrated in the results.

claim: Context is proposed to require an interplay between bottom-up and top-down information processing in distributed neural networks.
source: In the brain, context is proposed to require an interplay between bottom-up and top-down information processing in distributed neural networks (Tononi and Edelman, 1997; Friston, 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior theoretical work.

claim: The neural mechanisms underlying contextual information processing have been studied in visual perception, emotion, language, and social cognition.
source: the neural mechanisms underlying contextual information processing have been studied in a variety of domains including visual perception (Bar, 2004; Schwartz et al., 2007), emotion (De Gelder, 2006; Barrett et al., 2007; Barrett and Kensinger, 2010), language (Hagoort, 2005; Aravena et al., 2010), and social cognition (Ibañez and Manes, 2012).
evidence: Multiple citations support this claim about prior research domains.

claim: A 128-channel hemisphere-wide high-density electrocorticography array was used to quantify neuronal interactions with high spatial, spectral, and temporal resolution.
source: we used a 128-channel hemisphere-wide high-density electrocorticography (HD-ECoG) array to quantify neuronal interactions with high spatial, spectral, and temporal resolution.
evidence: The methods section describes the technical specifications of the recording system.

claim: The ECoG system has wider spatial coverage than conventional ECoG and LFP.
source: This ECoG system has wider spatial coverage than conventional ECoG and LFP (Buschman and Miller, 2007; Pesaran et al., 2008; Haegens et al., 2011)
evidence: This is a comparative claim supported by citations to prior work.

claim: The ECoG system has higher spatial resolution than MEG.
source: higher spatial resolution than MEG (Gross et al., 2004; Siegel et al., 2008)
evidence: This is a comparative claim supported by citations.

claim: The ECoG system has broader bandwidth than EEG.
source: broader bandwidth than EEG (Hipp et al., 2011)
evidence: This is a comparative claim supported by citation.

claim: The ECoG system has superior temporal resolution to fMRI.
source: superior temporal resolution to fMRI (Rees and House, 2005; Freeman et al., 2011)
evidence: This is a comparative claim supported by citations.

claim: Three monkeys participated in the study, one with a right hemisphere array (Subject 1), and two in the left hemisphere (Subjects 2 and 3).
source: Three monkeys participated, one with a right hemisphere array (Subject 1), and two in the right (Subjects 2 and 3)
evidence: This is a factual description of the experimental subjects.

claim: Six different video clips were created from three contexts combined with two responses.
source: Six different video clips were created from three contexts, vM threatened by a human (Ch), threatened by another monkey (Cm), or facing an empty wall (Cw), combined with two responses, vM showing a frightened expression (Rf), or neutral expression (Rn), which were termed ChRf, CmRf, CwRf, ChRn, CmRn, and CwRn
evidence: This describes the experimental design and stimulus conditions.

claim: When the context was perceived (C+) and the response stimulus was Rf, subjects focused more on the right section during the Response period.
source: When the context was perceived (C+) and the response stimulus was Rf, subjects focused more on the right section during the Response period, indicating interest in the curtain, or the threat behind the curtain, than the frightened vM (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is supported by eye tracking data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Gaze direction preference required not only the vM response, but also perception of the preceding context.
source: This is behavioral evidence that gaze direction preference required not only the vM response, but also perception of the preceding context, which demonstrated a cognitive association between the perception of the context and response stimuli.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the eye tracking data showing differential gaze patterns.

claim: Gazing behavior showed both response dependence (Rf > Rn) and context dependence (Cm ≈ Ch > Cw), but only when context was perceived (C+ > C−).
source: These results indicated that the subjects' gaze shift during the Response period showed both response dependence (Rf > Rn) and context dependence (Cm ≈ Ch > Cw), but only when context was perceived (C+ > C−).
evidence: This is supported by statistical comparisons of gaze positions shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Independent component analysis (ICA) was used to identify cortical areas over the 128 electrodes in the array.
source: To analyze the large-scale ECoG dataset, we identified cortical areas over the 128 electrodes in the array by independent component analysis (ICA).
evidence: This describes the analytical method used, with results shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Direct directed transfer function (dDTF) was used to measure the causality of a connection from one cortical area to another.
source: We then measured the causality of a connection from one cortical area (source area) to another (sink area) with a multivariate effective connectivity measure based on Granger causality: direct directed transfer function (dDTF) (Korzeniewska et al., 2003)
evidence: This describes the connectivity analysis method with citation to the original method.

claim: Parallel factor analysis (PARAFAC) extracted five dominant structures from the 3D tensor with consistency greater than 80%.
source: Parallel factor analysis (PARAFAC) extracted five dominant structures from the 3D tensor with consistency (>80%, also see Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by the core consistency diagnostic shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: Structure 1 was activated first, with context dependence only in the Context period (Cm > Ch > Cw) suggesting sensory processing that can discriminate between contextual stimuli.
source: Structure 1 was activated first, with context dependence only in the Context period (Cm > Ch > Cw) suggesting sensory processing that can discriminate between contextual stimuli, that is, context perception.
evidence: This is supported by the functional analysis shown in Figure 4A for Structure 1.

claim: The spectral dynamics of Structure 1 emerged primarily in the high-γ band (>70 Hz).
source: The spectral dynamics of Structure 1 emerged primarily in the high-γ band (>70 Hz)
evidence: This is shown in the dynamics panel of Figure 4B for Structure 1.

claim: Structure 1 contained mostly bottom-up connections from the posterior to anterior parts of temporal cortex.
source: and contained mostly bottom-up connections from the posterior to anterior parts of temporal cortex.
evidence: This is shown in the anatomical connectivity analysis in Figure 4C for Structure 1.

claim: Structure 2 was the earliest activated in the Response period, with only response dependence (Rf > Rn), and was independent of whether context stimuli were visually perceived (C+ ≈ C−).
source: Structure 2 was the earliest activated in the Response period, with only response dependence (Rf > Rn), and was independent of whether context stimuli were visually perceived (C+ ≈ C−).
evidence: This is supported by the functional analysis shown in Figure 4A for Structure 2.

claim: Structure 2 emerged in both high-γ and β bands.
source: Spectrally, Structure 2 emerged in both high-γ and β bands
evidence: This is shown in the dynamics panel of Figure 4B for Structure 2.

claim: Structure 2 corresponds to sensory processing that can discriminate between response stimuli, that is, response perception.
source: Thus, Structure 2 corresponds to sensory processing that can discriminate between response stimuli, that is, response perception.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the functional properties of Structure 2.

claim: Structure 3 was activated the second earliest in the Context period showing a generalized context dependence (Cm ≈ Ch > Cw) representing the abstract categorization of the context.
source: Structure 3 was activated the second earliest in the Context period showing a generalized context dependence (Cm ≈ Ch > Cw) representing the abstract categorization of the context ('an indeterminate agent is threatening vM').
evidence: This is supported by the functional analysis shown in Figure 5A for Structure 3.

claim: Structure 3 appeared mainly in the β band (10–30 Hz).
source: Structure 3 appeared mainly in the β band (10–30 Hz)
evidence: This is shown in the dynamics panel of Figure 5B for Structure 3.

claim: Structure 3 contained primarily bottom-up connections from the posterior temporal cortex (mainly the area TEO) to the anterior temporal cortex (mainly the temporal pole) and the lateral and medial PFC.
source: and contained primarily bottom-up connections from the posterior temporal cortex (mainly the area TEO) to the anterior temporal cortex (mainly the temporal pole) and the lateral and medial PFC.
evidence: This is shown in the anatomical connectivity analysis in Figure 5C for Structure 3.

claim: Structure 4 showed the same generalized context dependence as Structure 3, but during the Response period when context stimuli were absent and only in C+Rf.
source: Structure 4 showed the same generalized context dependence as Structure 3, but during the Response period when context stimuli were absent and only in C+Rf (not in C+Rn and C−).
evidence: This is supported by the functional analysis shown in Figure 5A for Structure 4.

claim: Structure 4 exhibited spatial and spectral characteristics similar to Structure 3.
source: Moreover, Structure 4 exhibited spatial and spectral characteristics similar to Structure 3 (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by correlation analysis shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Structure 3 corresponds to the initial formation/encoding of the contextual information, while Structure 4 represents the Rf-triggered reactivation/retrieval of the contextual information.
source: Structure 3 corresponds to the initial formation/encoding of the contextual information, while Structure 4 represents the Rf -triggered reactivation/retrieval of the contextual information.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the temporal and functional properties of Structures 3 and 4.

claim: Structure 5 showed context dependence (Cm ≈ Ch > Cw) in C+Rf and response dependence (Rf > Rn) in C+ during the Response period.
source: Structure 5 showed context dependence (Cm ≈ Ch > Cw) in C+Rf (not in C+Rn and C−), and response dependence (Rf > Rn) in C+ (not in C−) during the Response period
evidence: This is supported by the functional analysis shown in Figure 5A for Structure 5.

claim: Structure 5 appeared mainly in α and low-β bands (5–20 Hz).
source: and appeared mainly in α and low-β bands (5–20 Hz).
evidence: This is shown in the dynamics panel of Figure 5B for Structure 5.

claim: Structure 5 showed primarily top-down connections between posterior temporal cortex, the anterior temporal cortex, and the lateral and medial PFC.
source: Anatomically, the structure showed primarily top-down connections between posterior temporal cortex, the anterior temporal cortex, and the lateral and medial PFC.
evidence: This is shown in the anatomical connectivity analysis in Figure 5C for Structure 5.

claim: Structure 5 is the only one demonstrating clear top-down connections, with the same context and response dependence as the gaze behavior.
source: Remarkably, Structure 5 is the only one demonstrating clear top-down connections, with the same context and response dependence as the gaze behavior (see Figure 2B).
evidence: This is supported by comparison of Structure 5 properties with behavioral data in Figure 2B.

claim: Structure 5 corresponds to a network for the context-dependent feedback modulation of eye gaze or visual attention during the task.
source: These results suggest that Structure 5 corresponds to a network for the context-dependent feedback modulation of eye gaze or visual attention during the task
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the top-down connectivity and behavioral correlation of Structure 5.

claim: Structure 1 significantly correlated to Structures 3 and 4 across contexts in Rf.
source: Across contexts in Rf (Figure 6A, left), Structure 1 significantly correlated to Structures 3 and 4
evidence: This is shown in the functional coordination analysis in Figure 6A.

claim: Structures 3 and 4 were significantly correlated to Structure 5 across contexts in Rf.
source: which were themselves significantly correlated to Structure 5.
evidence: This is shown in the functional coordination analysis in Figure 6A.

claim: A significant correlation was found only between Structures 1 and 3 across contexts in Rn.
source: However, across contexts in Rn (Figure 6A, middle), a significant correlation was found only between Structures 1 and 3.
evidence: This is shown in the functional coordination analysis in Figure 6A.

claim: Structure 2 significantly correlated to Structure 4 across responses.
source: Across responses (Figure 6A, right), Structure 2 significantly correlated to Structure 4
evidence: This is shown in the functional coordination analysis in Figure 6A.

claim: Structure 4 was significantly correlated to Structure 5 across responses.
source: which was itself significantly correlated to Structure 5.
evidence: This is shown in the functional coordination analysis in Figure 6A.

claim: Significant correlations in temporal dynamics were found between structures activated in the Context period (Structures 1 and 3) and the Response period (Structures 2, 4, and 5).
source: Significant correlations in temporal dynamics were found between structures activated in the Context period (Structures 1 and 3) and the Response period (Structures 2, 4, and 5) (Figure 6B, left).
evidence: This is shown in the dynamic co-activation analysis in Figure 6B.

claim: Significant correlations in spectral profiles were found among structures with β band activation (Structures 2, 3, 4, and 5).
source: Significant correlations in spectral profiles were found among structures with β band activation (Structures 2, 3, 4, and 5) (Figure 6B, right).
evidence: This is shown in the dynamic co-activation analysis in Figure 6B.

claim: The numbers of shared connections between all structures were particularly high (>70% shared) between Structures 3 and 4 (abstract contextual information), and Structures 1 and 2 (perception).
source: The numbers of shared connections between all structures were particularly high (>70% shared) between Structures 3 and 4 (abstract contextual information), and Structures 1 and 2 (perception).
evidence: This is shown in the anatomical overlap analysis in Figure 6C.

claim: Pathways shared by all structures and subjects were found in and from the temporal cortex to PFC.
source: We examined the undirected pathways that exclude the directionality of connections and found pathways shared by all structures and subjects in and from the temporal cortex to PFC (Figure 6D, top).
evidence: This is shown in the anatomical overlap analysis in Figure 6D.

claim: Context can be represented by dynamic communication structures involving distributed brain areas and coordinated within large-scale neuronal networks.
source: In this study, we demonstrate that context can be represented by dynamic communication structures involving distributed brain areas and coordinated within large-scale neuronal networks, or neurocognitive networks (Varela et al., 2001; Fries, 2005; Bressler and Menon, 2010; Siegel et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a summary conclusion supported by the experimental findings and cited theoretical frameworks.

claim: Context can be encoded in large-scale bottom-up interactions from the posterior temporal cortex to the anterior temporal cortex and the lateral and medial PFC.
source: These findings show that context can be encoded in large-scale bottom-up interactions from the posterior temporal cortex to the anterior temporal cortex and the lateral and medial PFC.
evidence: This is supported by the anatomical connectivity patterns of Structure 3.

claim: The PFC is an important node in the 'context' network.
source: The PFC is an important node in the 'context' network (Miller and Cohen, 2001; Bar, 2004)
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: The lateral PFC is believed to be critical for establishing contingencies between contextually related events.
source: where the lateral PFC is believed to be critical for establishing contingencies between contextually related events (Fuster et al., 2000; Koechlin et al., 2003)
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: The medial PFC is involved in context-dependent cognition and conditioning.
source: and the medial PFC is involved in context-dependent cognition (Shidara and Richmond, 2002) and conditioning (Fuster et al., 2000; Koechlin et al., 2003; Frankland et al., 2004; Quinn et al., 2008; Maren et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Abstract contextual information can be encoded not only within the PFC, but in PFC interactions with lower-level perceptual areas in the temporal cortex.
source: Our results indicate that abstract contextual information can be encoded not only within the PFC, but in PFC interactions with lower-level perceptual areas in the temporal cortex.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the connectivity patterns observed in Structure 3.

claim: Brain contextual processing, from initial perception to subsequent retrieval, is represented not by sequential activation but rather sequential modular communication among participating brain areas.
source: Evidently, brain contextual processing, from initial perception to subsequent retrieval, is represented not by sequential activation but rather sequential modular communication among participating brain areas.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on the temporal and functional properties of the five structures.

claim: The network structures represent a module of modules, or 'meta-module' for brain communication connectivity.
source: Thus, we believe that the network structures we observed represent a module of modules, or 'meta-module' for brain communication connectivity.
evidence: This is a theoretical interpretation based on the hierarchical organization of the structures.

claim: Deficits in context processing in psychiatric disorders such as schizophrenia and post-traumatic stress disorder could contribute to their etiology.
source: Further investigation of this meta-structure organization for brain network communication could help determine how deficits in context processing in psychiatric disorders such as schizophrenia (Barch et al., 2003) and post-traumatic stress disorder (Milad et al., 2009) could contribute to their etiology.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about potential clinical implications, supported by citations.

claim: The five network structures' activity coordinated with each other in a deterministic manner, despite being highly overlapping in time, frequency, and space.
source: The relationships among network properties in the functional, temporal, spectral, and anatomical domains revealed network structures whose activity coordinated with each other in a deterministic manner (Figure 7A), despite being highly overlapping in time, frequency, and space (Figure 7B).
evidence: This is supported by the coordination analyses shown in Figure 6 and summarized in Figure 7.

claim: Multiplexed, large-scale neuronal network structures could represent a novel meta-structure organization for brain network communication.
source: Such multiplexed, yet large-scale, neuronal network structures could represent a novel meta-structure organization for brain network communication.
evidence: This is a theoretical interpretation based on the observed properties of the structures.

claim: The latent network structures were extracted computationally and will require further confirmatory experiments to verify their biological significance.
source: However, we caution that the latent network structures we identified were extracted computationally, and therefore will require further confirmatory experiments to verify their biological significance, particularly the causality of the connectivity patterns within each structure and the functional links bridging different structures.
evidence: This is an acknowledgment of the limitations of the computational approach.

claim: The biological meaning of the identified network structures could be achieved by selective manipulation of neuronal pathways by electrical or optogenetic stimulation linked to the ECoG array by neurofeedback, or neuropharmacological manipulations.
source: The biological meaning of the identified network structures could be achieved by selective manipulation of neuronal pathways by electrical or optogenetic stimulation linked to the ECoG array by neurofeedback, or neuropharmacological manipulations.
evidence: This is a suggestion for future experimental validation.

claim: The general class of network structures identified are not necessarily unique to context.
source: The general class of network structures we identified are not necessarily unique to context
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the generalizability of the findings.

claim: The approach of pooling large-scale data across subjects may be useful to extract network structures that are generalizable.
source: Our approach of pooling large-scale data across subjects may be useful to extract network structures that are generalizable, because neural processes specific to individual subjects or trials will cancel.
evidence: This is a methodological claim about the benefits of the analytical approach.

claim: The stable and consistent trial responses across subjects suggest that the network structures isolated may be candidate innate, elemental units of brain organization.
source: Indeed, the stable and consistent trial responses across subjects in our chronic ECoG recordings suggest that the network structures we isolated may be candidate innate, elemental units of brain organization.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation based on the consistency of findings across subjects.

claim: Future identification of unique differences in network structures between subjects could offer insight into structures related to individual trait and state variability, and the network-level etiology of brain diseases.
source: Conversely, future identification of unique differences in network structures between subjects could offer insight into structures related to individual trait and state variability, and the network-level etiology of brain diseases (Belmonte et al., 2004; Uhlhaas and Singer, 2006).
evidence: This is a speculative statement about potential future applications, supported by citations.

claim: Customized 128-channel ECoG electrode arrays containing 2.1 mm diameter platinum electrodes with an inter-electrode distance of 5 mm were chronically implanted in the subdural space in three Japanese macaques.
source: Customized 128-channel ECoG electrode arrays (Unique Medical, Japan) containing 2.1 mm diameter platinum electrodes (1 mm diameter exposed from a silicone sheet) with an inter-electrode distances of 5 mm were chronically implanted in the subdural space in three Japanese macaques (Subjects 1, 2, and 3).
evidence: This is a factual description of the experimental materials and methods.

claim: In Subject 1, electrodes were placed to cover most of the lateral surface of the right hemisphere, also the medial parts of the frontal and occipital lobes.
source: In Subject 1, electrodes were placed to cover most of the lateral surface of the right hemisphere, also the medial parts of the frontal and occipital lobes.
evidence: This is a factual description of electrode placement.

claim: In Subject 2, a similar layout was used, but in the left hemisphere.
source: In Subject 2, a similar layout was used, but in the left hemisphere.
evidence: This is a factual description of electrode placement.

claim: In Subject 3, all electrodes were placed on the lateral surface of the left hemisphere, and no medial parts were covered.
source: In Subjects 3, all electrodes were placed on the lateral surface of the left hemisphere, and no medial parts were covered.
evidence: This is a factual description of electrode placement.

claim: All experimental and surgical procedures were performed in accordance with the experimental protocols approved by the RIKEN ethics committee and the recommendations of the Weatherall report.
source: All experimental and surgical procedures were performed in accordance with the experimental protocols (No. H24-2-203(4)) approved by the RIKEN ethics committee and the recommendations of the Weatherall report, 'The use of non-human primates in research'.
evidence: This is a statement about ethical compliance.

claim: During the Waiting period, a still picture created by pixel-based averaging and randomizing all frames of stimuli was presented without sound for 2.5 s.
source: During the Waiting period, a still picture created by pixel-based averaging and randomizing the all frames of stimuli was presented without sound for 2.
evidence: This is a factual description of the experimental procedure.

claim: During the first 0.5 s of the Context period, a still image of an actor (a monkey) and an opponent (a monkey, a human, or wall) was presented with the sound associated with the opponents.
source: During the first 0.5 s of the Context period, a still image of an actor (a monkey) and an opponent (a monkey, a human, or wall) was presented with the sound associated with the opponents.
evidence: This is a factual description of the experimental procedure.

claim: The curtain closing animation took 0.5 s, and the curtain stayed closed for another 0.5 s.
source: The curtain closing animation took 0.5 s, and the curtain stayed closed for another 0.5 s.
evidence: This is a factual description of the experimental procedure.

claim: During the Response period, one of two emotional expressions of the actor (frightening or neutral) was presented with sound for 3 s.
source: During the Response period, one of two emotional expressions of the actor (frightening or neutral) was presented with sound for 3 s, followed by the Waiting period of the next trial.
evidence: This is a factual description of the experimental procedure.

claim: Cerebus data acquisition systems were used to record ECoG signals with a sampling rate of 1 kHz.
source: Cerebus data acquisition systems (Blackrock Microsystems, USA) were used to record ECoG signals with a sampling rate of 1 kHz.
evidence: This is a factual description of the recording equipment and parameters.

claim: Trials during which the subject's eye position was within the screen area more than 80% of the time during the first 0.5 s of the Context period were classified as C+ trials.
source: Trials during which the subject's eye position was within the screen area more than 80% of the time during the first 0.5 s of the Context period were classified as C+ trials.
evidence: This is a factual description of the trial classification criteria.

claim: The 50 Hz line noise was removed from raw ECoG data by using the Chronux toolbox.
source: The 50 Hz line noise was removed from raw ECoG data by using the Chronux toolbox (Bokil et al., 2010).
evidence: This is a factual description of the preprocessing method.

claim: The data was downsampled four times, resulting in a sampling rate of 250 Hz.
source: The data was then downsampled four times, resulted in a sampling rate of 250 Hz.
evidence: This is a factual description of the preprocessing method.

claim: The model order for ICA was determined by the PCA of the data covariance matrix, where the number of eigenvalues accounted for 90% of the total observed variance.
source: The model order, that is, the number of components, for ICA was determined by the PCA of the data covariance matrix, where the number of eigenvalues accounted for 90% of the total observed variance.
evidence: This is a factual description of the model order selection method.

claim: ICA was performed in multiple runs using different initial values and different bootstrapped data sets by using the ICASSO package with the FastICA algorithm.
source: ICA was performed in multiple runs using different initial values and different bootstrapped data sets by using the ICASSO package (Himberg et al., 2004) with the FastICA algorithm (Hyvärinen and Oja, 1997), which could significantly improve the reliability of the results (Meinecke et al., 2002).
evidence: This is a factual description of the ICA method with citations.

claim: The length and the step size of the sliding-window for segmentation were set as 250 ms and 50 ms, respectively.
source: The length and the step size of the sliding-window for segmentation were set as 250 ms and 50 ms, respectively.
evidence: This is a factual description of the analysis parameters.

claim: In all subjects, a model order of nine samples (equivalent to 9 × 4 = 36 ms of history) resulted in minimal AIC and was selected.
source: In all subjects, a model order of nine samples (equivalent to 9 × 4 = 36 ms of history) resulted in minimal AIC and was selected.
evidence: This is a factual description of the model order selection result.

claim: dDTF was calculated by using the Source Information Flow Toolbox (SIFT) together with other libraries.
source: dDTF (Korzeniewska et al., 2003), a VAR-based spectral connectivity measure, was calculated by using the Source Information Flow Toolbox (SIFT) (Delorme et al., 2011) together with other libraries, such as Granger Causal Connectivity Analysis (Seth, 2010) and Brain-System for Multivariate AutoRegressive Timeseries (Cui et al., 2008).
evidence: This is a factual description of the analysis tools with citations.

claim: False discovery rate (FDR) control was used to correct for multiple comparisons in multiple hypothesis testing, and a threshold of αFDR = 0.05 was used.
source: False discovery rate (FDR) control was used to correct for multiple comparisons in multiple hypothesis testing, and a threshold of αFDR = 0.05 was used.
evidence: This is a factual description of the statistical correction method.

claim: PARAFAC was performed by using the N-way toolbox, with no constraint on the first tensor dimension, and non-negativity on the second and the third tensor dimensions.
source: PARAFAC was performed by using the N-way toolbox (Andersson and Bro, 2000), with the following constraints: no constraint on the first tensor dimension, and non-negativity on the second and the third tensor dimensions.
evidence: This is a factual description of the PARAFAC analysis parameters with citation.

claim: The convergence criterion was set to be 1e-6.
source: The convergence criterion, that is, the relative change in fit for which the algorithm stops, was set to be 1e-6.
evidence: This is a factual description of the analysis parameter.

claim: The initialization method was set to be DTLD (direct trilinear decomposition) or GRAM (generalized rank annihilation method), which was considered the most accurate method.
source: The initialization method was set to be DTLD (direct trilinear decomposition) or GRAM (generalized rank annihilation method), which was considered the most accurate method (Cichocki et al., 2009).
evidence: This is a factual description of the analysis method with citation.

claim: Seven cortical areas were manually determined: the visual (V), parietal (P), prefrontal (PF), medial prefrontal (mPF), motor (M), anterior temporal (aT), and posterior temporal (pT) cortices.
source: Seven cortical areas were first manually determined: the visual (V), parietal (P), prefrontal (PF), medial prefrontal (mPF), motor (M), anterior temporal (aT), and posterior temporal (pT) cortices.
evidence: This is a factual description of the anatomical regions of interest.

claim: Trial shuffling was performed 50 times.
source: Trial shuffling was performed 50 times.
evidence: This is a factual description of the statistical validation procedure.

claim: The data are fully accessible online and can be downloaded from the website Neurotycho.org.
source: The data are fully accessible online and can be downloaded from the website Neurotycho.org.
evidence: This is a statement about data availability.
